nodes.question: How does the article suggest multi-level governance could contribute to the NSR?
nodes.answer: The article suggests that multi-level governance could assist in securing local effects, resolving disputes beyond trade, integrating member countries, and raising environmental sustainability within the NSR framework.
nodes.paragraph: The analysis reveals the potentials and challenges of the NSR for local effects but also includes suggestions for transnational cooperation and govern- ance, which finally leads to defining the role of supranational institutions and the necessity of local support in terms of a governance design. Although the initiative is partially successful, it requires further research on governance mechanisms for sustainable implementation. nodes.question: How does the article suggest that multi-level governance could assist in relation to the NSR?
nodes.answer: The article suggests that multi-level governance could assist in securing local effects, resolving disputes beyond trade, integrating member countries, and raising environmental sustainability through effective governance mechanisms.
nodes.paragraph: 2020). Scholars indicate and criticize the quality of institutional governance structures ( zt rk 2019), the definition of ownership (Du & Zhang 2018), efficacy and China S leadership towards a new international order (Beeson & Li 2016) and the risk of investment returns and participation (Tianren & Zhang 2021). In fact, the NSR requires an effective model of multi-level gov - ernance to resolve disputes beyond the trade perspective (Feldman 2018; Kettunen 2019), to integrate member countries (Boamah & Appiah-Kubi 2019) and to raise environmental sustainability (Coenen et al. 2020). Sustainability governance, there- fore, could act as a binding element across industries, combining supply chains and production networks to envision an international sustainable implementation of global activities (Bush et al. 2015) (Sect. 4.6). Sustainability along with the NSR is referred to as Chinas green BRI , which is also widely present in the state policies (Coenen et al. 2020; Defraigne 2021). However, it seems unauthentic as China is reallocating heavy industry to NSR countries and pushing climate neutrality far into the future.

nodes.label: Governance and participation
nodes.question: Who are some of the authors associated with the terminology and concepts of governance mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Key authors include Kooiman, Marin & Mayntz, Ansell & Gash, McQueen et al., Gonser & Schmid, Torng et al., and Evers & von Essen.
nodes.paragraph: The observation and analysis of alterations in gover- nance by increasing ways and new forms of participation especially but not only in liberal democratic systems and their political administrations, takes place in the theoretical literature under varying headings. The mention of newgovernance as modern governance (Kooiman, 1993 ) referred quite generally to altered relationships between state governance and the addressees in society. A centralconcept was that of cross-sectoral policy networks (Marin & Mayntz, 1991 ). In the subsequent international discus- sion, four terms have become established: collaborative governance (Ansell & Gash, 2007 ; Hofstadt et al., 2022 ), intersectoral governance (McQueen et al., 2013 ; Gonser & Schmid, 2023 ), interactive governance (Tor ng et al., 2019 ), and intermediation (Evers & von Essen, 2024 Despite all the differences in detail, there remains a greataf nity between these concepts. The common fundamental idea can be formulated as follows: They understand gov- ernance as a question of development and dealing withdifferent forms of mutual in uence and coordination between participants from the state sector, civil society, and the economy their involvement in the preparation ofconcepts, in decision-making, and in the process of their implementation.
